segments.t: Still at the apartment table, Max crunches on eggshells in Vika's pancakes and teases her until a playful food fight reveals she already finished her doctor's appointment that morning. Listen to the Russian exchange first.
Вика, не проще яйца без скорлупы добавить?
Я не повар, как ты.
То есть я, по-твоему, плохая жена?
Это не я сказал.
Вика, да чего, я пошутил!
Эй, тихо, тихо!
А ты обследование прошла или нет?
Ещё утром. А что это меняет?
Ой, мам, так жалко, что ты уезжаешь.
Нам без тебя будет так тяжело.
Нет, возвращаться плохая примета.
Папе привет, мы позвоним.
Now let's go back through their exchange line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Вика, не проще яйца без скорлупы добавить?

'Vika, wouldn't it be simpler to add eggs without the shells?' By checking whether not it be simpler to add eggs without the shells, Max presses Nastya for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Я не повар, как ты.

'I am not a professional chef like you.' Realizing that she is not a professional like Max changes how Vika handles the situation. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
То есть я, по-твоему, плохая жена?
'So in your opinion, am I a bad wife?' Over the table and the exchange, Vika presses Max for a straight answer.
Это не я сказал.

'I am not the one who said that.' Claiming that he is not the one who said sounds confident, even if Nastya has doubts. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
Вика, да чего, я пошутил!

'Vika, come on, I was only joking!' Once Nastya should come on he was only joking, Max makes sure Nastya hears every word. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Эй, тихо, тихо!
'Hey, easy, take it easy!' With the doctor and argument at stake, Max reacts without holding back.
А ты обследование прошла или нет?

'Wait, did you take your medical check-up or not?' Asking whether Nastya takes Nastya's medical check up or not is how Max puts Nastya on the spot. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Ещё утром. А что это меняет?

'Back this morning. What does that change?' Over the doctor and the exchange, Vika presses Max for a straight answer. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
Ой, мам, так жалко, что ты уезжаешь.
'Oh, Mom, it is such a pity you are leaving.' Realizing that Mom it is such a pity Max is leaving changes how Nastya handles the situation.
Нам без тебя будет так тяжело.

'It will be so hard for us without you.' Noting that it will be so hard for them without Max keeps Nastya's side of the story simple and clear. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Нет, возвращаться плохая примета.
'No, turning back is bad luck.' Even though turning back is bad luck, Nastya keeps a steady face in front of Max.
Папе привет, мы позвоним.
'Say hello to Dad, we will call.' By saying hello to dad they will call, Nastya keeps her side of the story grounded. Now let's hear the entire conversation once more from start to finish.
Вика, не проще яйца без скорлупы добавить?
Я не повар, как ты.
То есть я, по-твоему, плохая жена?
Это не я сказал.
Вика, да чего, я пошутил!
Эй, тихо, тихо!
А ты обследование прошла или нет?
Ещё утром. А что это меняет?
Ой, мам, так жалко, что ты уезжаешь.
Нам без тебя будет так тяжело.
Нет, возвращаться плохая примета.
Папе привет, мы позвоним.
That finishes Max and Vika's pancake argument and Nastya's farewell to her mother at the front door. Keep an ear out for comparative adverbs and family wishes. Until next time!
До свидания!
